briefs.polymarket-6563871: The question asks whether any Binance BTC/USDT one-minute candle from 12:00 AM ET on 2026-11-02 to 11:59 PM ET on 2026-11-08 has a low at or below $70,000. A Yahoo Finance wrap on the evening of 2026-11-02 said Bitcoin fell 1.92% to $76,732.38 as Binance withdrawals reopened after a $6.3 billion security breach (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/crypto-market-today-nov-2-223501665.html). Fortune reported about $77,750 at 6:30 a.m. ET that day (https://fortune.com/article/price-of-bitcoin-11-02-2026/). A November outlook piece cites a six-week low of $76,275, support watched at $76,000, and resistance at $80,181 and $82,000 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-price-outlook-november-2026-020000012.html). Binance users withdrew a net $3.64 billion on the Sunday reopening, and US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $515.03M in October, their first monthly outflow since June. From about $76,700, the $70,000 line is roughly 8.7% lower. No count of past seven-day windows with that deep a drawdown was found, and the Binance kline data could not be reached. For orientation, daily moves of 2-2.5% give a weekly spread near 6%, and a touch of a level 9% away within about six days is a modest-sized tail event. The downtrend, the exchange-specific stress on the very venue that resolves the question, and the ETF outflows make that tail somewhat fatter than usual. On the other side, price held the $76,000 area after the hack shock and withdrawals reopened without a collapse. All figures come from unopened search summaries, and the Nov 2 low and Nov 3 price are unknown. A fresh shock, such as a further exchange problem or a macro surprise around the US election and a possible FOMC meeting that week, would raise the odds, while a reclaim of $80,000 would lower them.

briefs.polymarket-3566406: The question resolves on the headline quarter-on-quarter growth rate in the ONS first quarterly estimate for July to September 2026, scheduled for 12 November 2026, to one decimal place; the band is 0.4% to 0.5% inclusive (https://www.financecalendar.com/?p=2217). The first estimate for Q2 2026 was +0.4% quarter on quarter and +1.2% year on year, and Q1 2026 was 0.6%. Monthly GDP for August 2026, published 2026-10-15, was +0.1% against a Reuters poll for a 0.1% fall; July was unrevised at +0.4% and June was revised up to 0.4% from 0.3% (https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/uk-economy-grows-01-in-august-defying-forecasts-of-a-decline). The ONS reported growth of 0.7% in the three months to August, with production up 0.8% in August, services flat and construction down 0.2% (https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/grossdomesticproductgdp/bulletins/gdpmonthlyestimateuk/august2026/pdf). Deutsche Bank on 2026-10-08 had expected a flat August and said momentum was slowing, and August then came in at +0.1% (https://www.tmgm.com/es/analysis/market-news/article/united-kingdom-gdp-momentum-seen-slowing-deutsche-bank-202610081200). The April and May monthly levels were not found, so the carry-over is approximate. Rough arithmetic with a flat September gives Q3 averaging about 0.6-0.8% above Q2, and this is not an official figure. Each 1% change in September moves the quarter by about a third of a point, so reaching the band would take a September fall of roughly half a percent or more, or downward revisions to July and August. A reference point on revisions is an average gap of 0.27 percentage points between first and final estimates since 2000. Recent quarterly prints have mostly been 0.1-0.7%, which makes the band a plausible but not central outcome. No consensus for Q3 and no Bank of England Q3 forecast had been published at the time of the research. A weak September print would be the main thing that moves the answer toward the band, and a flat or positive September would move it clearly above.
briefs.manifold-02RzZt8EII: The question resolves yes if, in any 2026 US Senate race, a candidate has 50.1% or more in the final Silver Bulletin polling average and loses the election. Newsweek, citing Silver Bulletin as of about 2026-10-23, reported Turek (D) at 46.8% against Hinson (R) at 45.6% in Iowa, Hamilton (D) trailing Marshall (R) by 1.1 points in Kansas, Brown (D) ahead of Husted (R) by 3.7 in Ohio, and Peltola (D) ahead of Sullivan (R) by 3.5 in Alaska (https://newsweek.com/who-will-win-the-midterms-what-polls-show-10-days-out-12610772). The same sources put the Silver Bulletin forecast at about a 76-78% chance of Democratic Senate control. Silver has said Texas and Maine are a normal-sized polling error away from flipping (https://www.natesilver.net/p/nate-silver-2026-midterm-election-senate-model). The state-by-state averages were not retrieved, so it is not known whether any candidate is at 50.1% or more, or whether independents such as those in Nebraska or Maine are included. No count of past cases was found; the reference class would be final polling-average leaders at or above 50% in Senate races from 2010 to 2024. In competitive races both candidates are usually in the mid-40s, so few contested races would qualify. Leaders above 50% are mostly in lopsided safe seats, where a loss takes a polling miss of a size seen only rarely. The route to a yes is a correlated polling error of several points, as in Maine and Iowa in 2020, hitting a race where a leader sits just over 50%. The election takes place on 2026-11-03, so the result will be known within days of the resolution date. The final average on the resolution date is the one used, and late polls could move it. What would change the answer is a list showing several competitive races with a leader above 50%, or an early sign of a large polling miss on election night.
briefs.manifold-tpR2hI2R8t: The question asks whether Joe Biden dies before 7 November 2028, a window of about two years from now. In a later statement, dated around early 2026 but not confirmed, he said the radiation worked as intended and also that the cancer is very painful and very debilitating, and he gave no prognosis (https://www.scrippsnews.com/health/joe-biden-says-radiation-treatment-for-prostate-cancer-worked-as-intended). Hunter Biden said in an August of unverified year that the cancer had gotten worse. Biden is 83 and turns 84 on 2026-11-20, and he has been active, working on a memoir. The reference class is men aged about 83 to 86 with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with androgen deprivation plus radiation. From general knowledge, with no source opened, median survival in that group is several years and roughly 30-40% survive five years. The baseline all-cause mortality for a US man of 83-84 is roughly 8-10% a year, which gives about 17-19% over two years before any cancer effect. Aggressive bone-spread disease raises this above the age baseline, while a treatment response and the slow course of hormone-sensitive disease lower it. No health news from the past week was found, and current PSA, imaging and treatment status are unknown. Reports of a new progression, hospitalization or change of treatment would raise the answer, and reports of stable disease would lower it.
briefs.manifold-gzgcNgtOqC: The question resolves yes if the 2026 US midterms, held 2026-11-03, are determined to be free and fair, and no if credible evidence shows systematic violations that materially affected the outcome or legitimacy; it closes on 2026-11-05. The OSCE has observed 12 federal campaigns since 2002, including six midterms, and found the process fundamentally sound each time; the 2024 mission found a well-run process with 31 recommendations (https://www.foreign.senate.gov/press/dem/release/ranking-member-shaheen-condemns-unprecedented-move-to-block-international-observers-from-us-midterm-elections). Mid-decade redistricting is another contested factor. The short window to 2026-11-05 comes before any final report, so documented systematic violations are unlikely to exist by then, but the criteria are broad and list intimidation and unlawful orders, which leaves room for the resolver's reading. No polls or election-day incident reports were found. Election-day incident reports, a court ruling on the mail-voting order, or a formal assessment from a domestic monitor would change the answer.
